business: Abora Automation (sets up a missed-call SMS/WhatsApp reply and enquiry summaries for trade businesses)
target: Owners of small trade businesses in Germany (plumbing/heating, electrical, roofing, painting, carpentry, landscaping) who are on site all day and miss calls
notes: ALL GUESSES by the founders' assistant, not data: shares, incomes and behaviours are estimates. Only real input so far: founders say most enquiries come by phone; one owner called was close to retirement and not interested.

segments.name: Established business, 6-15 employees, partner or office help does the phone

behaviours.name: Overbooked
behaviours.how: Has more work than time; a missed call barely hurts because the order book is full for months.

behaviours.name: Growth-minded younger owner
behaviours.how: Took over or founded the business recently, uses WhatsApp and Google, wants more and better jobs.

behaviours.name: Tech sceptic
behaviours.how: Avoids new software, distrusts anything with 'KI', buys only what a colleague recommends.

behaviours.name: Penny pincher
behaviours.how: Counts every monthly fee, cancels subscriptions he does not use.

behaviours.name: Wife/partner does the office
behaviours.how: A family member answers the phone part-time and does quotes in the evening.

behaviours.name: Near retirement
behaviours.how: Plans to stop or hand over within a few years and avoids new commitments.

behaviours.name: Emergency trade
behaviours.how: Many urgent calls (burst pipe, heating failure); a slow reply loses the job to the next number on Google.

objections: My customers want to talk to a person, not get a text message
I call back anyway in the evening, I don't lose jobs
149 euros a month is a lot for an SMS
I don't want to change my phone setup or my number
Data protection: who reads my customers' messages?
Never heard of you, two guys without customers
Many callers are older people with a landline who can't receive SMS or WhatsApp
I already have too much work
habits: you are on a ladder or under a sink most of the day with dirty hands
you listen to the mailbox in the van at lunch
you do quotes on Sunday evening at the kitchen table
your customers find you via Google Maps and word of mouth
you use WhatsApp with suppliers and some customers
